'''Gennadii Vladimirovich Belyi''' (1951–2001, {{langx|uk|Генадій Володимирович Білий}}, {{langx|ru|Геннадий Владимирович Белый}}) was a [[Soviet Union|Soviet]], [[Ukrainian people|Ukrainian]], and [[Russian people|Russian]] mathematician, known for [[Belyi's theorem]] on the representation of [[algebraic curve]]s as [[Riemann surface]]s and for the Belyi functions arising in that theorem.

Belyi was born on February 2, 1951, in [[Magnitogorsk]], [[Russia]], then part of the [[Soviet Union]]. His family moved from there to [[Ukraine]], and he began his studies at the [[Ukrainian Physics and Mathematics Lyceum|Kiev Physics and Mathematics School]] but moved from there to [[Moscow State University]]. After completing his studies in 1973 he returned to Ukraine, working in [[Kiev]] and then [[Lviv]]. He became a graduate student at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] in Moscow in 1975, and studied there under the supervision of [[Igor Shafarevich]], earning a candidate degree in 1979. He then took a faculty position at [[Vladimir State University]], in [[Vladimir, Russia|Vladimir]], Russia, where he remained for the remainder of his career. He died on January 29, 2001, in Vladimir.<ref name="bdikps">{{citation

Surveys'' '''57''' (5): 981–983, {{doi|10.1070/RM2002v057n05ABEH000554}}.</ref><ref>{{citation|publisher=Kiev Mathematical Society|url=http://www.mathsociety.kiev.ua/Bilyi_G.html|accessdate=2012-09-07|title=Belyi Gennady, 1951 – 2001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161116162253/http://www.mathsociety.kiev.ua/Bilyi_G.html|archive-date=2016-11-16|url-status=dead}}.</ref>

Belyi won a prize of the [[Moscow Mathematical Society]] in 1981, and was an [[list of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers|invited speaker at the International Congress of Mathematicians]] in 1986.<ref name="bdikps"/>
